labels.notes: Kind research, no label, no mark claimed: the module docstring says 'no ledger row is certified here' and has no **`label`** mark. The quote matches l.788-790 verbatim. Lean >= target block, checked one hypothesis at a time. GX.GammaP.isElliptic_or_eq_one_of_timelike takes only hp : minkQ p < 0 (both sheets of H^2_pm, the strict sign convention minkQ = -t^2 + |x|^2), theta : TpHS p ≃ₗ[ℝ] ℂ (any theta, oriented or not) and A : GammaP p (GammaP is a subgroup of Causal.Flat.lorentz 2, which is SO_0(1,2): preserves Q, future-causal, det 1). It concludes GX.PSL2.IsElliptic (pslMk (gammaToSL p theta A)) ∨ pslMk (gammaToSL p theta A) = 1. #print confirms IsElliptic is the strict GX.PSL2.IsElliptic (trSq < 4) of GX/BBS/RP1Circles.lean:979. This is exactly the disjunction HSSingularities.lean:1977 states. 'Rotation of the Euclidean plane p^⊥' is tangent_isRotation_of_timelike, which is basis-free: Q∘dsProj is positive definite on T_pHS^2, its polar form is preserved, det = 1. With range_dsProj (dsProj onto p^⊥) and the strict dsProj_injective, this is SO(p^⊥). The sharpening pslMk(...) = 1 ↔ A ∈ {1, gammaHalfTurn} (pslMk_gammaToSL_eq_one_iff_of_timelike) is true, and gammaHalfTurn_ne_one makes it non-trivial. No statement is vacuous: a time-like p exists. SCOPE (a) discloses that the paper's '1-parameter elliptic subgroup' is not formalized; SCOPE (b) names the OQ-113 (b)/(d) dependence. No reading is taken for the single-element statement, which holds under either reading of (d).

labels.notes: No mark claimed. The quote matches l.797-799 verbatim. Lean >= target block. tangent_isUnipotent_of_null (hp : minkQ p = 0, hA : A ≠ 1) proves T − id ≠ 0 and (T − id)^2 = 0, i.e. unipotent and ≠ 1. smul_eq_iff_of_null (same hypotheses) proves A • σ = σ ↔ σ ∈ tangentDirs p. That set has exactly two elements by the strict ncard_tangentDirs, so 'fixes no ray but the two tangent directions' holds as a set equality. isParabolic_iff_of_null (hp, any theta, any A) proves GX.PSL2.IsParabolic (pslMk (gammaToSL p theta A)) ↔ A ≠ 1, with the strict notion (trSq = 4 ∧ ≠ 1, RP1Circles.lean:982), an iff stronger than the target. No added hypothesis. The paper's 'Γ_p generated by a parabolic element' is not formalized. SCOPE (a) discloses this and the REPORT raises it as a question, with the reading 'every element ≠ 1 is parabolic' named.

findings_and_questions_checked: Finding l.789-790 is true. Under OQ-113 (b), the double-cover structure that linkToRP1 encodes, the half-turn about a time-like p has tangent action −id (tangent_gammaHalfTurn), so gammaToSL gives −I and pslMk(−I) = 1 (pslMk_gammaToSL_eq_one_iff_of_timelike, proved). The half-turn is not 1 (gammaHalfTurn_ne_one, proved). A (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-circle with holonomy ρ = half-turn therefore has central PSL-holonomy through the bridge toPSL f = pslMk (gammaToSL θ ρ). The argued example, a cone point of angle π, is right, because a rotation by α has image R_α in SL(2,ℝ), which is central exactly when α ∈ πℤ. The finding is correctly conditioned on OQ-113 (b) (under the visual reading the half-turn would be an elliptic involution) and correctly routed to OQ-113 (d). Injectivity at a light-like p is proved (pslMk_gammaToSL_eq_one_iff_of_null).

Question l.798 (and l.794-795) is true. At a null p, the pointwise stabiliser of p in SO_0(1,2) is the group of null rotations, ≅ ℝ, and so is not cyclic. The file's lemmas support this: gammaToSL is injective at a null p, and every tangent action is unipotent, fixing the tangent line pointwise (tangent_eq_self_of_null), so Γ_p embeds in the upper-unipotent group ≅ ℝ. At a spacelike p the stabiliser is SO_0(1,1) ≅ ℝ. It is properly a question, not a finding, with the reading named ('every element ≠ 1 is parabolic', which is what isParabolic_iff_of_null proves). The argument is not formalized, and the REPORT says so.
